correctness.rationale: For every prime power q and n, perfectness makes all natural squares independent and every automorphism monomial. The exact fixed equations t_i²M_{σi,σj}=t_jM_{ij} yield codimension ≥ceil(s(2n−s)/2) for permutation support s≥2. For σ=id with s exotic scalings, disjoint forced-zero entry sets give codimension ≥s(n−s)+s²/(q−2)≥sn/(q−2). Union/expectation bounds conditioned on GL_n, then Burnside, establish the explicit stated error and limiting class count, including q=2. Two exhaustive independent implementations verified all maps and small cases for q=2,3 and n=2,3. Finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A recent survey identifies random automorphism probabilities and classification counts as mathematical directions; the theorem resolves a natural infinite-dimensional regime, quantitatively explains asymptotic freeness of the monomial action, and determines the first-order class-number growth from an otherwise expensive Burnside sum. Its explicit error also makes the statement nontrivial even when the existing exact orbit formula is known. Fixed q, invertible matrices and the unsharp constant are stated limitations.
